description: 20-12's behavioural proof for the `## Creating images and video` body section added alongside it, and the fixture owed by CLAUDE.md's playbook rule 'teach a tool, owe a fixture' now that `dispatchMedia` is in the body. Turn 1 asks for a short promo video in ordinary language and DELIBERATELY never names the tool — a turn that said 'use dispatchMedia' would be a compliance test, not a routing one. `mediaDispatchCount: 1` is graded off `agentSteps`, so it fails on the exact defect no reply assertion can catch: the agent answering in prose ('I'll put a reel together for you') while never calling the tool. Equality rather than a floor is also load-bearing — a SECOND dispatch on the same thread recycles the single `plans.by_thread` row the first proposal is still being written into (`stageMediaPlan`'s `dispatch_in_flight` interlock), so 'exactly one' is the assertion and a floor would pass on the bug. NOTE for whoever reads this next: TWO actors write a `dispatchMedia` step on this thread — the agent's tool call, and `dispatch.ts`'s record of the SPECIALIST RUN it schedules (`tool: resolved.spec.stepTool`, `stepKey: dispatch:<rootRequestId>`). The observable excludes the second, which run 420c852b discovered the expensive way: this fixture failed 'expected 1, got 2' while the agent had called the tool exactly once. `agentSteps.test.ts` now pins that filter offline. `recipientCount: 0` and `attachmentCount: 0` are the teeth on the other half of the contract: a video request must never be reframed as an email, which is exactly what the v2 body's 'Route by intent, not by habit' section claims. `statusAtMost: proposed` allows the staged media card and refuses anything further — the harness never clicks Generate, so no provider job, no render and no media spend can exist on this run.
turns: We just finished the benchmark-MD1 rebrand — can you put together a short promo video for it? Something punchy I can post vertically.
